title: House
description: A configured house: rooms, each of a type, with its slots bound or left empty. The whole point of the product is that this is the only thing a user writes, and even this is largely generated from what they plug in. 1.0.0 required at least one room, which made rooms a prerequisite for having a house rather than the first thing a person adds to one: a house with no areas in Home Assistant could not be set up at all, and the sidebar panel -- which registers when a config entry exists -- was never reachable. This version removes that floor. A house of no rooms is a house that has been made and has nothing in it yet, which is exactly the state a person is in the moment they finish setup in a home that has no areas; the panel is where the rooms are added afterwards. Nothing else changes: `rooms` keeps 1.0.0's item shape, and `house_scope` was already allowed to be empty.

house_scope.description: Slots that belong to the house rather than a room, so a house-scoped behaviour is not forced through a room type it has nothing to do with.

slots.description: Slot names made available at house scope.

type.description: The name of a room type. Resolved against room_types.yaml.

bindings.description: Slot name to binding. A slot the type provides may be absent, which is how an optional slot is left unbound.

registry_id.description: The device registry id, when the binding is a device rather than a bare entity.
